text:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding sample app failing on edge runtime (Vercel Edge) with SDK v2.3.1. Observed auth retry loops and 401s only on edge; node and local dev are fine.

sam: repro steps?

maria: clone repo, yarn, run `vercel dev --edge` or deploy. Error shows: token refresh request gets 401, SDK retries forever until function times out.

kyle: I reproduced. Looks like the edge bundle is pulling the wrong entry from package exports. In the built bundle there's a reference to `lib/cjs/*` instead of the ESM/edge entry.

jen: Do we still ship an `exports` map with conditional fields like "edge", "worker", "import", "require"?

maria: yes. package.json exports currently: 

```json
{
  "exports": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
    "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

maria: but bundlers/runtime are picking `import` instead of `edge` when running on Vercel Edge. The `import` build still does Node-specific fetch/auth stubs that call the server-side token refresher (which fails in edge env).

sam: hmm. does the edge field exist at the root export or nested subpath? Some resolvers only honor conditional exports for the package root; others ignore subpath conditions.

kyle: it's at the root only. I think the problem is how Vercel (and esbuild/rollup configs used by sample apps) resolve the conditional order — they prefer `import` over `edge` unless `edge` is explicitly requested by consumer bundler config.

jen: That means our sample app's rollup/esbuild config needs to prefer the `edge` condition when targeting worker runtime. But we can't rely on every user's bundler doing that. We should publish a compatibility note and a small patch: add an `exports` order with `edge` before `import` or add an `browser` style fallback for edge.

maria: Proposed PR: reorder to `edge`, `import`, `require`, `default` and add a small edge-specific entrypoint that throws at runtime if used in Node. Also call out in samples how to force `conditions: ["edge"]` in build config for esbuild.

sam: Any typing issues? TS users reported types resolving to cjs `index.d.ts` sometimes.

kyle: Yes — TypeScript's `types` resolution ignores conditional exports; we currently point `types` at `dist/types/index.d.ts` but our package splits types into `types/esm` and `types/edge` for slightly different signatures (edge omits some Node-only overloads). When bundler picks wrong runtime entry, types can mismatch actual runtime behavior and trigger auth/retry confusion in generated code.

maria: Repro gist: deploy sample with `target: 'experimental-edge'` and the runtime logs show: `AuthError: token refresh not implemented for runtime` coming from `dist/esm/auth.js` while expected implementation is in `dist/edge/auth.mjs`.

jen: Quick mitigation: patch package.json on npm to make `edge` the first condition. That will likely fix Vercel and Cloudflare workers that respect conditional exports.

kyle: Agreed. Also add a short snippet in the sample README: how to set `conditions: ['edge']` for esbuild and how to pin the SDK version.

sam: Could we also change the default `import` build to detect `globalThis.EdgeRuntime` and call through to edge implementation? That might be more hacky but would cover mis-resolves.

maria: I'd prefer a clear exports ordering + docs + tests. Add a CI job that runs the sample against a local edge emulator (vercel dev for edge) to catch regressions.

ci-bot: New issue created: #4523 "conditional exports order causes edge auth retry failures" (severity: medium)

jen: Owner?

maria: I'll open the PR and tag kyle for the types changes. Sam can follow up with sample config edits.

kyle: Will also add a TypeScript smoke test that imports the package in `moduleResolution: 'node16'` and `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` modes to ensure consistent types.

sam: Plan and timeline?

maria: PR today that reorders exports + README note. CI change and TS tests early next week. If we see no major regressions, release patch and publish sample update.

jen: Sounds good. Also ping support to notify any users who reported similar errors.

maria: Thanks all — going to start the PR. :thumbsup:
